sources.entry: Samba | Free software re-implementation of the SMB/CIFS networking protocol

summary.one_liner: Samba is a free, GPL-licensed suite that implements the SMB/CIFS networking protocol so Linux/Unix servers can provide Windows-compatible file and print services and integrate with Active Directory.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Samba as the standard Windows interoperability suite for Linux and Unix. It provides file and print services to clients using the SMB/CIFS protocol, including DOS, Windows, OS/2 and Linux clients. It can run as an Active Directory domain controller or as a regular domain member. The README points to a full HOWTO for the AD DC implementation and to a wiki for documentation. It also covers contribution workflow via GitLab and the project's mailing lists. The README is mostly project governance and community information, so it says little about specific build steps or configuration.
use_cases: share files between Linux and Windows machines
join a Linux server to an Active Directory domain
run a Samba-based Active Directory domain controller
replace a Windows file server with a Linux one
notable: Can act as an Active Directory domain controller or a domain member
Free software under the GNU General Public License
Has been providing file and print services since 1992
Project is a member of the Software Freedom Conservancy
caveats: The README gives no install or build instructions; setup details are in the external HOWTO and wiki
Domain controller setup requires following a separate full HOWTO
keywords: samba alternative to windows file server
